---
name: ha-evershelf-budget-workflow
description: Thin budget-aware Home Assistant EverShelf integration workflow preserving complete service wiring, backend ownership, capability/idempotency tests and HACS release requirements.
---

# Integration budget workflow

Use global `budget-workflow` and `.github/agent-budget.json` when available.
Shared tools live under `$HOME/.copilot/skills/budget-workflow/scripts/`.
If unavailable, use direct symbols/ranges and the same bounded workflow.
For substantive retained-owner work, resolve one exact entry from
`.github/agent-opportunities.json` with the shared `opportunities.mjs` planner.
Registered zero-model validation commands are declared in
`.github/agent-tools.json`. All opportunities use hierarchical version 3
definitions. The version 3 release machine remains disabled while GitHub
Release, archive/HACS verification, rollback and cleanup drivers are
unavailable.
Its deterministic route and tools apply only to that opportunity. The entire
project remains disabled because the case packet is invalidated. When
replacement evidence exists, known patterns use the exact medium coordinator;
research, specification, and critical review require named trigger receipts.

Use `evidence/research.mjs plan` with the adapter's `evidencePolicy`. Existing
schema/handler questions are repository-only; external HA semantics with local
wiring are hybrid; unrelated public questions are neutral external-only.
Prefer current-owner `init`/`evidence`. Inspect both registered schema and shared
builder before a hybrid contract; they can differ on null/key-presence rules.
Open authoritative external gap evidence before returning for applicability.
No automatic reader agent or inferred backend execution guarantee.

1. Read the root service/release contract. Follow the entire service boundary,
   not just the visible handler. Use `test_recipe_api.py` and
   `test_recipe_services.py` as focused behavioral evidence.
2. Mechanical wiring may use one standard implementation owner. Novel
   capability, authorization, error, or idempotency behavior requires stronger
   reasoning and explicit state/outcome cases.
   The adapter defines a provisional bounded-model lane for low-risk focused
   tests, but admission remains disabled because the prior evidence packets
   were incomplete and contribute zero valid cases toward the required 30.
   Any future candidate must use complete evidence, clean exact targets, and
   the qualified network-off pytest sandbox with read-only dependency mounts
   and no host environment. Provisional output has no application authority.
   Cross-surface service semantics and registration,
   capability, authentication, idempotency, or live HA work remain with the
   owner; scaffolds and existing-file transforms also stay with the owner.
3. Keep catalog business logic in EverShelf. Keep responses bounded and
   credentials out of URLs, logs, prompts, and evidence.
4. Run affected pytest files/selectors together. Include unload/registration,
   capability failure, replay, transient backend, and todo-mirror behavior
   when affected. Revise once from failures; escalate once if necessary.
5. No live HA service calls as a unit-test shortcut. Release only when
   explicitly approved; a tag alone is not a completed HACS release. Routine
   release coordination uses Sol high/default for static version, changelog,
   workflow, tag, GitHub Release, and HACS checks. Escalate to max/long only
   when those artifacts conflict, HACS visibility remains ambiguous after the
   normal indexing window, or rollback safety cannot be established.
   The version 3 `.github/release-machine.json` remains disabled until its
   deterministic GitHub Release, artifact/HACS verification and rollback
   drivers are fault-tested. Routine release review is Sol medium/default;
   max/long requires `haes-hacs-release-conflict`. Only explicit operator
   authorization can start deterministic release execution.

No implicit tandem and no second HydraFusion layer under the coordinator.
The current overall model never bypasses exact project pins and gains no
semantic, apply, live, or release authority from orchestration alone.

The default learning observer follows `.github/agent-learning.json`, records
only sanitized prompt-scoped operation/receipt metadata, and may use
`automaticBuild: true` for one exact local incubation owned by the selected
opportunity's medium coordinator. The invalidated cheap-worker packet still
prevents that worker launch; it does not disable medium-owned incubation.
`automaticPromotion: false` remains unchanged, and credentials, live HA/HACS
and release remain excluded.
